verses.zh: 論 尼 尼 微 的 默 示 ， 就 是 伊 勒 歌 斯 人 那 鴻 所 得 的 默 示 。
verses.en: This is an oracle[NOTE:1] about Nineveh; the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite:[NOTE:2]
notes: See note at Isa 13:1.
Or “Nahum of Elkosh” (NAB, NRSV).

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 是 忌 邪 施 報 的 神 。 耶 和 華 施 報 大 有 忿 怒 ； 向 他 的 敵 人 施 報 ， 向 他 的 仇 敵 懷 怒 。
verses.en: The Lord is a zealous[NOTE:1] and avenging[NOTE:2] God;the Lord is avenging and very angry.[NOTE:3] The Lord takes vengeance[NOTE:4] against his foes;he sustains his rage[NOTE:5] against his enemies.
notes: See note at Isa 13:1.
Or “Nahum of Elkosh” (NAB, NRSV).

Heb “jealous.” The Hebrew term קַנּוֹא (qannoʾ, “jealous, zealous”) refers to God’s zealous protection of his people and his furious judgment against his enemies. The root קָנָא (qanaʾ) can denote jealous envy (Gen 26:14; 30:1; 37:11; Pss 37:1; 73:3; 106:16; Prov 3:31; 23:17; 24:1, 19; Ezek 31:9), jealous rivalry (Eccl 4:4; 9:6; Isa 11:13), marital jealousy (Num 5:14, 15, 18, 25, 30; Prov 6:34; 27:4), zealous loyalty (Num 11:29; 25:11, 13; 2 Sam 21:2; 1 Kgs 19:10, 14; 2 Kgs 10:16; Ps 69:10; Song 8:6; Isa 9:6; 37:32; 42:13; 59:17; 63:15; Zech 1:14; 8:2), jealous anger (Deut 32:16, 21; Ps 78:58), and zealous fury (Exod 34:14; Deut 5:9; 29:19; 1 Kgs 14:22; Job 5:2; Pss 79:5; 119:139; Prov 14:30; Isa 26:11; Ezek 5:13; 8:3; 16:38, 42; 23:25; 35:11; 36:5, 6; 38:19; Zeph 1:18). See BDB 888 s.v. קָנָא; E. Reuter, TDOT 13:47-58.

The syntax of this line has been understood both as a single clause (NRSV, NASB, NIV) and as two parallel clauses (KJV). The LXX reflects the latter, “God is jealous, and the Lord avenges.” Masoretic accentuation and Hebrew syntax support the former, that is, the accentuation links קַנּוֹא וְנֹקֵם (qannoʾ venoqem, “jealous and avenging”) together. Normal word order suggests that קַנּוֹא וְנֹקֵם (“jealous and avenging”) are attributive adjectives modifying אֵל (ʾel, “God”) and that the Lord is the subject. Another possibility is that the adjectives are a case of hendiadys and should be understood as “The Lord is a zealously avenging God.”

Or “exceedingly wrathful”; Heb “a lord of wrath.” The idiom “lord of wrath” (וּבַעַל חֵמָה, uvaʿal khemah) means “wrathful” or “full of wrath” (Prov 22:24; 29:22). The noun “lord” (בַעַל) is used in construct as an idiom to describe a person’s outstanding characteristic or attribute (e.g., Gen 37:19; 1 Sam 28:7; 2 Kgs 1:8; Prov 1:17; 18:9; 22:24; 23:2; 24:8; Eccl 7:12; 8:8; 10:11, 20; Isa 41:15; 50:8; Dan 8:6, 20); see IBHS 149-51 §9.5.3.

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 不 輕 易 發 怒 ， 大 有 能 力 ， 萬 不 以 有 罪 的 為 無 罪 。 他 乘 旋 風 和 暴 風 而 來 ， 雲 彩 為 他 腳 下 的 塵 土 。
verses.en: The Lord is slow to anger[NOTE:1] but great in power;[NOTE:2] the Lord will certainly not[NOTE:3] allow the wicked[NOTE:4] to go unpunished.He marches out[NOTE:5] in the whirlwind and the raging storm; dark storm clouds billow like dust under his feet.[NOTE:6]

verses.en: The mountains tremble before him;[NOTE:1] the hills convulse;[NOTE:2] the earth is laid waste[NOTE:3] before him;the world and all its inhabitants[NOTE:4] are laid waste.[NOTE:5]

verses.en: No one can withstand[NOTE:1] his indignation![NOTE:2] No one can resist[NOTE:3] his fierce anger![NOTE:4] His wrath is poured out like volcanic fire,boulders are broken up[NOTE:5] as he approaches.[NOTE:6]
notes: See note at Isa 13:1.

verses.en: Surely they will be totally consumed[NOTE:1] like[NOTE:2] entangled thornbushes,[NOTE:3] like the drink of drunkards,[NOTE:4] like very[NOTE:5] dry stubble.
notes: See note at Isa 13:1.
